clue.text: The look that kills?

parts.note: in rhyming slang a '... hook' rhymes with 'look', and those who slaughter animals for meat are the ones that kill

explanation.surface: A deadly glare, the kind of look said to kill.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang shortens 'butcher's hook' (look) to its first word, so 'have a butcher's' means 'have a look'; the question mark flags the second reading, the slaughterers themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang for a glance, and also the tradespeople who slaughter livestock.

clue.text: So-called plot by fence causes hullabaloo

indicators.note: so-called here means as it is called aloud, a word that sounds like another

parts.note: to brew something up is to plot it
a ha-ha is a sunken fence or ditch bounding a park

explanation.surface: A scheme hatched by a receiver of stolen goods sparks an uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fence' suggests a receiver of stolen goods; it is the HA-HA, a ditch with a wall used in English country estates instead of a visible fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy fuss or commotion, a synonym.

clue.text: Treat harshly girl one's overwhelmed with old port

indicators.note: pieces overwhelmed by another are engulfed inside it

parts.note: Tyre is an ancient Phoenician seaport
Ann is a girl's name
one is I, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A girl is mistreated, swamped by an old fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink; it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule or behave like a despot, oppressing people.

clue.text: Landlords of little houses on both sides of the street

indicators.note: a piece on both sides of another wraps round it

parts.note: ho. is the short form of house, so HOS is houses abbreviated

explanation.surface: Property owners with cottages lining both sides of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Innkeepers who receive guests, publicans or hoteliers.

clue.text: Caruso, you said, could be this. Surely not!

definitions.text: Caruso, you said, could be this. Surely not!

indicators.note: what the letters could be is another arrangement of them
the word said aloud is the letter U

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like U

explanation.surface: Was the great tenor Caruso harsh-voiced, as you claimed? Surely not!
explanation.walkthrough: 'you said' gives U, its sound; CARUSO plus U are rearranged. The whole clue defines too, with 'Surely not!' protesting the slur.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh and loud in sound, which the famous tenor's voice never was.

clue.text: Castle, some say, was involved in battle

indicators.note: what some people say out loud signals a word that sounds like the one before it

parts.note: a castle is a fort, a fortified stronghold

explanation.surface: A castle, according to some, saw action in a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of wage war: to have been engaged in combat.

clue.text: Alternative date entered for surgical treatment

indicators.note: a piece that has entered another is placed inside it

parts.note: an option is an alternative choice
an era is a date in the sense of a period

explanation.surface: A substitute appointment is booked for an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A procedure performed by a surgeon on the body.

clue.text: Theatre-in-the-round

parts.note: Shakespeare's circular London playhouse, whose name is also a word for a sphere or round world

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's open-air circular playhouse, named after a spherical model of the world.

clue.text: Compact sort of port

definitions.meaning: a compact is a formal agreement between parties
a harbour opened to foreign trade by international agreement

explanation.definitionFit: An agreement between nations, and the kind of Chinese harbour opened to foreign trade by such an accord.

clue.text: At first, smoked fish stink…

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Smoked fish starts to smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A foul smell, a synonym.

clue.text: At heart regrets being swallowed by very large man-eaters

indicators.note: one piece being swallowed puts it inside the other

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label meaning very large

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central part, so only the middle letters of regrets are used

explanation.surface: Gigantic man-eaters secretly regret what they have swallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At heart' here takes the central three letters, not just the single middle one; OS (outsize) is a clothing-label convention for very large.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy-tale giants are monsters who devour people.

clue.text: Crazy flag here

definitions.meaning: a British slang phrase meaning mad or confused
a flag is flown at the top of a flagpole

explanation.definitionFit: British slang for deranged, and literally the spot where a raised flag sits on its mast.

clue.text: Passes on easily

definitions.meaning: to bequeath or hand on to a later generation
winning with no effort at all, an idiom from horse racing

explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb for bequeathing to heirs, and an idiom for winning without effort.

clue.text: Prevent a surgeon getting right inside

indicators.note: one piece getting inside another is placed within it

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon

explanation.surface: Stopping a surgeon from getting the right to operate inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To ward off or stop something happening, a synonym.

clue.text: A chap and I — abroad we appear utterly atrocious

parts.note: a chap is a man, referred to as he
nous is French for we, the word used abroad

explanation.surface: Two people on holiday confess they look appalling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' tells the solver to give 'we' in a foreign language, here French.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked or shocking in the extreme, a near synonym.

clue.text: …of smell that makes us cry? A lot of nonsense!

indicators.note: making nonsense of words jumbles their letters

explanation.surface: Something about smell makes us weep, which sounds like a lot of nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonsense' shuffles CRY plus A LOT OF; the dots carry on from the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective relating to the sense through which odours are perceived.

clue.text: Bluff Henry VIII

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance
VIII is the Roman numeral for eight

explanation.surface: Henry VIII was famously bluff, blunt and hearty in manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bluff' looks like an adjective for the king's manner; it is a noun, a steep cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluff is a steep headland or cliff, an elevated place.

clue.text: Most of term promises to be highly entertaining

indicators.note: most of a word drops its final letter

parts.note: Hilary is the spring term at Oxford and some other universities and law courts
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A student expects the coming term to be great fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremely funny, a synonym.

clue.text: Stews are getting cooked — they show reaction to heat

indicators.note: something cooked is changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Casseroles in the oven change as they warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting cooked' fits the stews in the kitchen; it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: People who perspire, as one does in hot weather.

clue.text: Smoking jacket?

parts.note: a short double-breasted sailor's coat shares its name with a cannabis cigarette, which one smokes

explanation.surface: An elegant lounging garment for after dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting naval jacket, and also slang for a joint that is smoked.

clue.text: Charm girl wearing spots

indicators.note: a piece wearing another is clothed in it, inside it

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots
Vi is a short girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl with spotted clothing is charming.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant or delight, an older sense of the verb.

clue.text: Former part of England and most of Wales out of control

indicators.note: letters out of control run wild into a new order
most of a word drops its last letter

explanation.surface: A political complaint that much of England and Wales is ungovernable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims WALES to WALE; with AND those letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The region of northern and eastern England once ruled by Viking settlers under their own law.

clue.text: One turned up in coloured dress — that's rotten!

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it

parts.note: a dress that has been coloured has been dyed

indicators.note: in a down clue a word turned up reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone appears in a brightly dyed frock that has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' suits a down clue, where reversed letters read upwards; 'coloured dress' describes the result of dyeing, the past-tense verb the wordplay needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Decomposed, gone bad, a synonym.

clue.text: Aquatic creature harms one U-boat, leaving the others alone

indicators.note: taking only every other letter leaves the remaining letters alone

explanation.surface: A sea creature damages a submarine, sparing the others.
explanation.walkthrough: The second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of HARMS ONE U-BOAT are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-celled water-dwelling organism that changes shape.

clue.text: Add in turn one, a hundred and a score

indicators.note: taken in turn here means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: to add is to sum
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A tally: add up one, a hundred and twenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks like twenty in the arithmetic, but it is the written notes of a composition.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is the written notation of a piece for performers.

clue.text: Foreign wife's endless complaint

indicators.note: endless drops the final letter of the word

parts.note: a squawk is a loud complaint

explanation.surface: A wife from abroad grumbles without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated, now offensive term for a Native American woman or wife.

clue.text: A form of service accepted by the state? The other way round

indicators.note: one piece accepted by another is taken inside it

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state

indicators.note: a new form of the word means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Public service recognised by the government, or perhaps it is the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the state' looks general but is a specific US state; 'A form of' is the anagram signal, and the shuffled service letters sit inside Virginia's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase meaning conversely, with the positions reversed.

clue.text: Five zero — about 50 — are very eloquent

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
O looks like zero
ca is short for circa, meaning about
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A score line reading five-nil with about fifty spectators is eloquent.
explanation.definitionFit: Outspoken, expressing views forcefully, a synonym.

clue.text: Bird in a very bad way — one left in competition

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

indicators.note: one having left means it departs from the word

parts.note: lousily means terribly, in a very poor manner
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bird in dreadful shape is the one left over in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one left' drops an I from LOUSILY, leaving LOUSLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Striving to equal or outdo a rival, the sense of eager rivalry.

clue.text: The end is nigh

definitions.meaning: a finish or conclusion, as of a day

explanation.surface: The doom-monger's cry that the end of the world approaches.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun for a conclusion, and an adjective meaning near at hand.

clue.text: Sailing boat comes back in, as ever

indicators.note: one piece put in another sits inside it
a word that comes back is read backwards

parts.note: a yawl is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A yacht returns to port, as it always does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' looks like part of the definition 'as ever', but it is the container; the definition is just 'ever'. 'comes back' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever in the sense of at all times, permanently, a synonym.

clue.text: Loves deeply, as one does when the first sign of love is involved

parts.note: I can stand for one, the first person

indicators.note: something involved is wrapped up inside another piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone describes adoring a person once love first shows itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one does' is read literally as I followed by DOES, ungrammatical on purpose; 'involved' puts the opening letter of love plus IS inside the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship someone as an object of devotion, to adore.
